facts: NASA SP-8119 states that metal alloys selected for contact with the system fluid shall be compatible with the system fluid and resistant to all anticipated forms of corrosion.
NASA SP-8119 lists chemical reaction (including reaction on impact that can cause ignition) between materials and the system fluid as a material-compatibility consideration.
NASA SP-8119 lists propellant decomposition (materials or contacts that cause propellant decomposition) as a material-compatibility consideration.
NASA SP-8119 lists corrosion modes—atmospheric, galvanic, and stress corrosion—as material-compatibility considerations.
NASA SP-8119 directs designers to consult the electrochemical series for dissimilar-metal selection and to consider platings and finishes when selecting materials for contact with system fluids.

NASA SP-8119 recommends preparing a list of suitable materials on the basis of the above compatibility, reaction, decomposition, and corrosion considerations (i.e., basing material selection on those evaluated factors).

NASA SP-8119 warns against using materials that can cause ignition or propellant decomposition in liquid-oxygen or similar environments (the guidance specifically references avoiding certain materials/contacts in those contexts).
